Second attributive article standing between the expressed head noun Ζαχαρίου and its participle; rule 31's test is whether the article governs an expressed head noun, and it does, so the article realizes nothing and the relativizer is the participle's helper, exactly as τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → *God who created* has it and as this chapter reads ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασα at 11:27, οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες at 11:44 and τὸ αἷμα … τὸ ἐκκεχυμένον at 11:50. Rule 90 was the earlier reading here and does not reach this configuration, saying in terms that it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed. That the name is anarthrous does not make the article substantival: rule 31's anarthrous-head clause (καρπὸν δικαιοσύνης τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ) is scoped to a following prepositional phrase, which has no verb to carry a relativizer, whereas a participle does. Reading τοῦ ἀπολομένου as a substantival apposition — *Zachariah, the one who perished* — and giving the article the *who* under rule 90 remains defensible, and is what the verse pass took.

review_notes: τοῦ ἀπολομένου is brought into line with 11:27, 11:44 and 11:50: the article is unrepresented under rule 31 and the participle carries *who perished*.

Rule 90 was cited by the verse pass and does not reach an article governing an expressed head noun; a proper name is such a noun, and rule 31's anarthrous-head clause is scoped to a prepositional-phrase modifier rather than to a participle.
All other units are unchanged from the accepted alignment.
